name: create_grants
description:
Creates one or more grants in a single transaction (all-or-nothing). Max **100** grants.

### Body fields
Each grant: `resourceType`, `subjectType`, `subjectId`, `roleId`, and **exactly one** of:
- `resourceId` — concrete resource id
- `resourceFqn` — concrete FQN, or a wildcard:
  - most resource types: full `*`
  - `provider-account`: **only** `{providerAccountCategory}:*` (e.g. `model-provider-accounts:*`). Bare `*` is **400**.
  - `provider-integration`: **only** `{integrationType}:*` (e.g. `model:*`). Bare `*` is **400**.
Tenant-admin does **not** bypass the bare-`*` ban on create. After resolve, allowed wildcards store `resourceId='*'` with the provided `resourceFqn` (so distinct wildcards stay distinct).

### Authorization
- **Resource:** `MANAGE` required on each distinct resolved `(resourceType, resourceId)` (for wildcards, MANAGE on `*`), unless the caller has `ASSIGN_ROLE` on the tenant
- **Assign role:** `ASSIGN_ROLE` allows grants on any resource type, including wildcards, without per-resource `MANAGE`
- **Wildcards:** require **tenant-admin** or `ASSIGN_ROLE`. User and team subjects are rejected; wildcards may only target agent or virtualaccount.
- **Provider-integration (concrete):** additionally require `MANAGE` on the parent provider-account, or tenant-admin, or `ASSIGN_ROLE`

### Subject aliases (folded before write)
- `agent` → stored as `agent-identity`
- `virtualaccount` → stored as `serviceaccount`

### Tenant storage
For `resourceType=tenant` with a non–`tenant-admin` role, the grant is stored on the caller **account**.

### Example — by resourceId
```json
{
  "grants": [{
    "resourceType": "mcp-server",
    "resourceId": "czveqmv31la7pkdxa09anf9f",
    "subjectType": "agent",
    "subjectId": "z9rcvwtau3g0m4o5kjoarlt0",
    "roleId": "mcp-server-manager"
  }]
}
```

### Example — by resourceFqn (resolved on backend)
```json
{
  "grants": [{
    "resourceType": "mcp-server",
    "resourceFqn": "truefoundry:mcp-server:openapi-client-cred-auth0-testing",
    "subjectType": "agent",
    "subjectId": "z9rcvwtau3g0m4o5kjoarlt0",
    "roleId": "mcp-server-manager"
  }]
}
```

grants.description: Non-empty batch of grants to create (max 100). All-or-nothing in one transaction.

resourceType.description: Resource to grant on. Allowlist enforced in validateCreateGrantsBody (400).

resourceId.description: Valid resource id (unique identifier). Provide exactly one of resourceId / resourceFqn. `resourceId: "*"` is rejected — send wildcards via `resourceFqn`.

resourceFqn.description: Resource FQN. Provide exactly one of resourceId / resourceFqn. Backend resolves before MANAGE + write. Concrete FQNs and partial wildcards are allowed; full `*` is allowed except on provider-account / provider-integration (use `{providerAccountCategory}:*` / `{integrationType}:*` instead, e.g. `model-provider-accounts:*` / `model:*`). Wildcards require tenant-admin.

subjectType.description: Subject receiving the grant. `agent` is stored as agent-identity; `virtualaccount` is stored as serviceaccount. Subject is not authorization-checked on create.

roleId.description: Role id. Must exist for the resource type being granted on. For resourceType=tenant, non–tenant-admin roles are stored on the caller account.

Apache Datafusion SQL query. Tables are accessed as "{dataRoutingDestination}"."{tableName}".

Available tables:
- traces: OpenTelemetry compliant traces enriched with AI Gateway columns
- gateway_feedbacks: User feedback (ratings, comments) linked to traces

- gateway_mcp_metrics: Metrics for MCP requests

name: list_grants
description:
Lists grants for either a **resource** (`resourceType`+`resourceId`)
or a **subject** (`subjectType`+`subjectId`) — exactly one mode pair.

### Top-level provenance / scope (optional)
- `source` — `AUTH_API` | `ROLE_BINDING` (not allowed inside JSON `filter`)
- `grantSourceScope` — `wildcard` | `direct` (not allowed inside JSON `filter`)

### JSON `filter` (optional)
Same allowlisted tree as v1 list filters, plus `resourceFqn`. Ops: EQUAL, IN,
NOT_IN, IS_NULL, STRING_CONTAINS, STRING_STARTS_WITH, STRING_ENDS_WITH.

Allowlisted fields: roleId, roleName, subjectId, subjectType, resourceId,
resourceType, roleBindingId, resourceFqn.

Example inline wildcards for model:*:
`source=AUTH_API&grantSourceScope=wildcard&filter={"op":"and","values":[{"field":"resourceFqn","op":"EQUAL","value":"model:*"}]}`

### Other query params
- `search` — case-insensitive OR over subjectSlug / resourceName /
  roleName / roleBindingName (≤500)
- `sortBy` — `subjectSlug`, `subjectType`, `resourceName`, `resourceId`,
  `resourceType`, `roleName`, or `roleId`; `sortOrder` defaults to `desc`
- `limit` / `offset` — default **100** / **0**

Tenant rows come first so inherited access reads above resource grants. `sortBy` orders
within a group, and `pagination.total` counts matches before paging.

### Subject aliases
- Query `agent` matches DB `agent-identity` **or** `agent-channel-identity`
- Query `virtualaccount` matches DB `serviceaccount`
- Response `subjectType` surfaces `agent` (not `agent-identity`)

### Auth
Grant rows expose who holds which role, so listing needs manage on the resource or subject.
- By resource: `MANAGE` on the resource. Concrete `provider-integration` / `vcs-integration`
  additionally require `MANAGE` on the parent provider-account (`USE_INTEGRATION` is not enough)
- By subject user: `MANAGE_USERS` on account
- By subject team: `MANAGE_TEAM`
- By subject agent: `subjectId` is the **agent-identity** id; allow if `MANAGE_AGENT` on the
  linked agent (e.g. agent-manager) **or** `MANAGE_AGENT_IDENTITIES` on account
- By subject VA: `MANAGE_VIRTUAL_ACCOUNT` including team-owned VAs when the caller has VA
  manage via the owning team (team-manager / team-member)

resourceType.description: By-resource mode: use with resourceId (XOR subjectType+subjectId).

resourceId.description: By-resource mode: resource id (`*` = wildcard rows for that type). Use with resourceType.

subjectType.description: By-subject mode: use with subjectId. Accepts `agent` (matches agent-identity or agent-channel-identity) and `virtualaccount` / `serviceaccount`.

subjectId.description: By-subject mode: subject id. Use with subjectType.

source.description: Top-level provenance filter. AUTH_API → source=AUTH_API AND roleBindingId IS NULL. ROLE_BINDING → source=ROLE_BINDING. Not allowed inside JSON `filter`.

grantSourceScope.description: Top-level wildcard vs direct filter. wildcard → resourceId=*; direct → resourceId<>*. Not allowed inside JSON `filter`.

filter.description: JSON list-filter tree (AND/OR). Allowlisted fields: roleId, roleName, subjectId, subjectType, resourceId, resourceType, roleBindingId, resourceFqn. Do not put `source` or `grantSourceScope` here — use the top-level query params. Same ops as v1: EQUAL, IN, NOT_IN, IS_NULL, STRING_*.

search.description: Case-insensitive substring OR across subjectSlug, resourceName, roleName, roleBindingName. Max 500 chars.

sortOrder.title: SortDirection
sortOrder.description: Sort direction when sortBy is set. Default desc.

name: revoke_grant
description:
Revokes exactly one inline (`AUTH_API`) grant. Role-binding (GitOps) grants are not matched (404).

### Body
Provide `resourceType`, `subjectType`, `subjectId`, `roleId`, and **exactly one** of:
- `resourceId` — concrete resources
- `resourceFqn` — concrete FQN, full `*`, or partial wildcard (`model:*`, `docker-registry:*`, …)

Bare `*` on `provider-account` / `provider-integration` can still be revoked (tenant-admin or `ASSIGN_ROLE`) so leftover rows from older manifests can be cleaned up. Create rejects those bare `*` grants.

### Authorization
- `MANAGE` on the resource (after resolve), unless the caller has `ASSIGN_ROLE` on the tenant
- `ASSIGN_ROLE` allows revoking a grant on any resource type, including wildcards, without per-resource `MANAGE`
- Wildcard revoke (`resourceId` resolves to `*`) requires **tenant-admin** or `ASSIGN_ROLE`
- Concrete provider-integration additionally requires **MANAGE** on the parent provider-account, tenant-admin, or `ASSIGN_ROLE`

### Subject aliases
- `agent` → matches DB `agent-identity`
- `virtualaccount` → matches DB `serviceaccount`

### Example — revoke user on agent resource
```json
{
  "resourceType": "agent",
  "resourceId": "xin2tvnektl5i0bz5y7l4fg7",
  "subjectType": "user",
  "subjectId": "cm1fa35mu009s0trd2q7l9o4",
  "roleId": "agent-manager"
}
```

### Example — revoke partial wildcard (model:*)
Stored as `resourceType=provider-integration`, `resourceId=*`, `resourceFqn=model:*`.
You must send `resourceFqn` (not `resourceId: "*`") so `*` and `model:*` are not confused.
```json
{
  "resourceType": "provider-integration",
  "resourceFqn": "model:*",
  "subjectType": "virtualaccount",
  "subjectId": "va-or-sa-id",
  "roleId": "provider-integration-access"
}
```

### Example — revoke agent identity grant (FE subjectType=agent)
```json
{
  "resourceType": "mcp-server",
  "resourceId": "czveqmv31la7pkdxa09anf9f",
  "subjectType": "agent",
  "subjectId": "z9rcvwtau3g0m4o5kjoarlt0",
  "roleId": "mcp-server-manager"
}
```

resourceId.description: Valid resource id (unique identifier). Provide exactly one of resourceId / resourceFqn.

resourceFqn.description: Resource FQN. Provide exactly one of resourceId / resourceFqn. Use for concrete FQNs, full wildcard `*` (including legacy provider-account / provider-integration `*` rows), or partial wildcards like `model:*` / `model-provider-accounts:*`.

subjectType.description: Subject type. User-facing only: `agent` (stored as agent-identity) and `virtualaccount` (stored as serviceaccount).

subjectId.description: Internal id of the subject (user id, team id, agent-identity id, or VA/serviceaccount id).

roleId.description: Role id of the grant to revoke.

name: sync_application
description: Trigger an Argo CD sync operation for the application when cluster objects are OutOfSync or a sync operation is stuck. The application must be running (not paused). Prefer redeploy_application when the user wants a new rollout from the current TrueFoundry deployment; use this when the desired state is already recorded but the cluster has drifted. This writes a new operationState (unlike clearing Application status, which can leave operationState empty).
